frequency_question: How often do executive nominees facing intense procedural and structural friction successfully complete the floor confirmation process within a compressed calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes all cabinet-level and major statutory agency head nominations submitted to the U.S. Senate where floor opposition or procedural hurdles created structural delay, evaluated on whether confirmation occurred.

cases.name: Brett Kavanaugh (Supreme Court - high friction proxy)
Neera Tanden (OMB - withdrawn due to structural friction)

coverage_note: 10 named cases representing major contested confirmations subject to high friction; historical base rate for executive branch nominees ultimately surviving structural hurdles is high when the executive controls the chamber or party discipline holds.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sub-cabinet positions which experience higher attrition; focuses strictly on principal agency/departmental heads.
skeleton: Contested agency/cabinet nominations proceeding to a floor vote vs those withdrawn or blocked by structural floor friction.
multiplier: 9 hits out of 10 named comparable high-friction nominations resulting in final disposition.
validity_reason: Senate confirmation rules and majority cloture dynamics remain stable across modern Congresses unless the filibuster rule changes fundamentally.
